root_cause: The drawer opens via show()/showModal() but focus is not programmatically moved into the dialog in the test environment, leaving keyboard users unable to reach the close button or form controls. Native showModal() auto-focus does not fire in JSDOM, and previous microtask/synchronous focus attempts in _showElement ran before the dialog was fully ready for focus.
repair_strategy: In DialogBase._showElement, after showing the dialog, queue a requestAnimationFrame callback to focus the first focusable element within the dialog. This ensures the dialog is fully rendered and in the top layer before focus is attempted, working for both modal and non-modal drawers in test and real browsers.
expected_accessibility_effect: When the drawer opens via keyboard (Enter on Filters button), focus moves to the close button (#filters-close) after the next paint, allowing sequential Tab navigation through all form controls (#in-stock, #waterproof, #apply) without a pointer.
functional_risks: If a dialog intentionally manages focus differently (e.g., expects focus on a specific element via autofocus), this could override that intention.
The focusable selector might not match all focusable element types (e.g., contenteditable, area, custom elements with tabindex).
If the dialog content is dynamically loaded, the first focusable element might not exist yet when the focus attempt runs.
verification_requirements: After pressing Enter on #filters-open, focus must be on #filters-close.
Subsequent Tab presses must move focus to #in-stock, then #waterproof, then #apply.
Escape key must close the drawer and return focus to #filters-open.
Clicking Show results must update the applied output correctly.
Ensure the drawer still opens/closes correctly for mouse users.
Modal dialogs (showModal) should continue to work with browser auto-focus where available.
